items.text: Rod Serling's The Twilight Zone premiered on CBS on October 2, 1959.
items.question: Who did you watch The Twilight Zone with, and is there one episode you still remember?
items.source_quote: October 2 — Rod Serling's classic anthology series The Twilight Zone premieres on CBS.

items.text: Postage for a domestic letter was 4 cents an ounce.
items.question: Where were you living when a stamp for a letter cost four cents, and who did you write to?

items.text: Bobby Darin's "Mack the Knife" spent nine weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in October and November 1959, the year's longest-running number one.
items.question: Where were you living when Bobby Darin's "Mack the Knife" was on the radio, and who in your house knew the words?
source_quote: The Billboard Hot 100 is a chart published since August 1958 by Billboard magazine which ranks the best-performing singles in the United States. In 1959, it was compiled based on a combination of sales and airplay data sourced from surveys of retail outlets and playlists submitted by radio stations respectively, and 16 different singles spent time at number one.
Bobby Darin spent nine non-consecutive weeks at number one in October and November with "Mack the Knife", making it the year's longest-running number one

items.text: Hawaii was admitted as the 50th U.S. state on August 21, 1959.
items.question: Where were you living when Hawaii became the 50th state, and who was the first person you knew to go there?
items.source_quote: August 21 — Hawaii is admitted as the 50th and last U.S. state (see History of Hawaii).

items.text: On April 9, 1959, NASA announced the Mercury Seven, seven military pilots chosen to become the first U.S. astronauts.
items.question: Do you remember seeing the first seven astronauts in the newspaper or on television, and which one did you follow?
items.source_quote: April 9 — NASA announces its selection of the "Mercury Seven", seven military pilots to become the first U.S. astronauts.
